name: Text as a whole
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a common system for the return of third-country nationals staying illegally in the Union, and repealing Directive 2008/115/EC of the European Parliament and the Council, Council Directive 2001/40/EC and Council Decision 2004/191/EC
part_text:
The European Parliament wants one set of rules across the EU for removing people who have no right to stay. Countries would have to issue a return decision quickly, and a decision made in one country could be enforced in another. People could be detained longer, up to 24 months, and those seen as security risks even longer. Appeals would not automatically pause removal. The rules also cover cooperation with countries outside the EU and returning people to them.

- **What changes:** One EU-wide return system, longer detention, shared decisions between countries, no automatic pause on removal when appealed.
- **Who it affects:** People staying in the EU without permission, and national authorities who remove them.
- **What happens next:** Parliament has set its position; talks with EU governments follow before any law is final.
